title: Say whether a held frame pushes the sound too
goal: Holding a frame makes the picture longer, and a voice track on its own layer carries straight on underneath it. That is right when you are talking over the frozen frame and wrong when the voice belongs to the shot, and at the moment there is no way to ask for the other one. Let the person say which, at the moment they freeze.
notes:
From hold-on-a-frame (2026-09-21). The freeze clickthrough (docs/design/mocks/pages/video-freeze-wt.html) has a segmented row in Properties called "The insert pushes" with Everything and Picture only, and its own closing question asks whether the timeline should show the drift. Only Picture only is built, because that is what falls out of the model: ClipPieces.holdFrame edits ONE layer's pieces, and every other layer with time stays where it is.

Reproduced, in the model, as a test that now pins the behaviour: Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/HeldFrameTests.swift, "A hold pushes the picture along, and sound on its own layer keeps running under it". It lays a sound layer at 0..8000 beside an eight second clip, holds a frame for five seconds, and asserts the sound layer's time is byte for byte what it was while the picture now ends at 13s.

  $ Scripts/test.sh --filter aHoldPushesThePictureOnly
  ✔ Test "A hold pushes the picture along, and sound on its own layer keeps running under it" passed after 0.001 seconds.

What "Everything" would mean is a ripple insert across the whole document rather than across one clip's pieces, which is why it is its own task rather than a flag on the freeze: every layer with an in past the hold moves by the hold's length, and a clip the hold lands INSIDE has to be cut. Worth settling what a title or a second clip does before building it.
acceptance: When a frame is held in a document that has sound on its own layer, the person can choose whether everything moves along or only the picture does
The choice is made where the freeze is made, not in a settings window, and it can be changed after the fact on the hold that is picked
Whichever is chosen, the timeline shows what happened: it is obvious at a glance whether the voice still lines up with the picture
A walk covers both choices and the exported file proves each one

log.note: Adversarial review before building. The mock's row ("The insert pushes: Everything / Picture only") is NLE jargon; building it literally hands a first-time user two words with no consequence attached. Building instead: one radio pair in the Time section, in the same idiom as "Hold for" right above it, worded as what you would HEAR ("Everything waits" / "The rest carries on") with a sentence naming the cost of each. Cut from the mock: the segmented control shape (inconsistent with the panel's own lists). Answering the mock's own open question the narrow way: the drift is drawn ONLY on a bar that runs under a hold that pushed the picture alone, so the common case stays clean. Default chosen: Everything, because a sound that silently slides five seconds out of step with the picture for the rest of the edit is the expensive, invisible error, while a pause in the voice over a frozen frame is obvious and one click away.

Built. Core: HoldPush.swift (the choice, the document-wide ripple, the drift readings) + the push flag on ClipPiece, 20 tests in HoldPushTests, whole suite green at 8972. App: a pair of circles in the Time section (SpeedInspector.whatItPushes) that sets the next freeze and changes the hold in hand, EditorState.holdPushChoice/setHoldPush, and the drift mark on ClipPiecesBar. Walk: hold-pushes-the-sound-walk, 44 steps, ok, 4 real window captures, and both exports measured (19s with everything waiting, 14s without). Ran the neighbours too: hold (8), sound (3), cut-on-the-timeline, an-edited-recording-comes-out-as-a-video, all ok.

Found and fixed by looking at the walk's own picture rather than at the tests: the silence a pushing hold inserts into a sound layer was itself an unmarked held piece, so it read as a hold that had pushed the picture alone and the timeline drew '5s out' on all three bars for an edit that drifted nothing. Inserted silence now carries push: .everything, and there is a test with two sound layers pinning it (silenceIsNotAHoldOfItsOwn).

left rough (none of these earned a task, and I searched 'hold pushes sound drift' and 'remembered between windows' first, which found only this task): (1) the drift hairline lands under the playhead straight after a freeze, so only the chip reads until you move the playhead; (2) what the next freeze pushes is remembered for the window and not across launches; (3) the drift mark is drawn on a title or an arrow spanning a picture-only hold too, where 'out of step' reads as a sound word; (4) a second video clip the hold lands inside gets a frozen frame of its own, pinned by a test but never watched by hand because the sample recording is one clip; (5) the clickthrough's segmented 'The insert pushes' row was deliberately not built as drawn.

The Time section now asks what a hold should push, where the freeze is made: Everything waits (the default, so a voice stays with its shot) or The rest carries on, changeable on the hold afterwards. A bar running under a picture-only hold carries an orange '5s out' at the hold. Core in HoldPush.swift with 20 tests; whole suite green at 8972; hold-pushes-the-sound-walk is ok with 4 real window captures and both exports measured (19s vs 14s); the hold, sound, cut and export walks re-run green. Shipped in 5a5a8db2. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-22-hold-pushes-the-sound.json
